texts.preamble: Mohammad Rafeeda Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 3 January, 2022 Author: A. Rajasheker Reddy Bench: A.Rajasheker Reddy, M. Laxman Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Rajasheker Reddy & Hon'Ble Sri Justice M. Laxman Wp No.15278 Of 2021 Order :
texts.facts: The detenu earlier committed four offences and again committed three more offences which amply demonstrates his habitual nature of committing crimes. Therefore the detenu has been labelled a "Goonda" as defined in Clause (g) of Section 2 of the Act and the detention order is passed. The Government accorded approval of the said detention order.
texts.arguments: Counter affidavit is filed by the 2nd respondent wherein inter- alia it is stated that the impugned order of detention terming the detenu as 'Goonda' has been passed having regard to his habitual indulgence in offences of attempt to murder, hurt and criminal intimidation in an organized manner Mohammad Rafeeda Begum vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 3 January, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83593067/ 1 and thereby he has been acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of "public order" apart from disturbing peace, tranquility and social harmony in the Society. That, there is no basis muchless any merit in the allegation that the detention order was passed in a mechanical manner. That, as there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in further such offences, the detention order was passed with a view to prevent him from indulging in such fresh offences. That the detention order was passed based on the material placed and on arriving at subjective satisfaction. That, recourse to normal law may not be an effective deterrent to prevent the detenu from indulging in such further activities which would be prejudicial to maintenance of the "public order" in the concerned area. That, the order of detention passed is an exercise of reasonable anticipation having regard to the criminal cases registered against the detenu. 06. Sri T. Niranjan Reddy, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the detaining authority while passing the impugned order did not consider the conditions of bail as imposed by the trial Court subjectively except making a cryptic reference that the detenu made persistent efforts to come out from the jail for which he moved several bail petitions, which the detenu under law is entitled to. Consideration of bail conditions before passing the detention order is held to be mandatory by the Division Bench of this Court in VASANTHU SUMALATHA vs. STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH (2015 SCC Online Hyd 790). 07. Learned Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of learned Addl. Advocate General, on the other hand, submitted that the detenu was enlarged on bail and there is every likelihood of the detenu involving in similar offences and the detenu has already been involved in series of same type of crimes, which are sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity and fear in the minds of the people at large, the impugned order of detention was passed on subjective satisfaction of the detaining authority. The issue of non consideration of conditions imposed in bail order was considered by this Court in Vasanthu Sumalatha and others vs. State of Andhra Pradesh [2015 SCC OnLine Hyd 790: (2016) 1 ALT 738(DB)], wherein it was held that non consideration of bail conditions imposed in bail orders vitiates the detention order on the ground of non application of mind.
